correctness.rationale: The CDF inversion and the formula Q_a′(u)=h(u^(1/a))/[u(-log u)] have been recomputed. Direct logarithmic differentiation gives h′/h=[1-(1-z)/(-log z)-z/(-log(1-z))]/[z(1-z)]<0 by two instances of log x<x-1. Since u^(1/a) increases with a for 0<u<1, quantile derivatives strictly decrease with a. Integration yields the full strict dispersive order. Uniform quantile coupling yields strictly ordered absolute pairwise differences, and finite moments ensure strict variance order. Standalone standard-library checker passed 2585 numerical assertions; finite checks are not treated as infinite proof. No unstated regularity or boundary limit is required.

value.rationale: The same probability family controls the previously studied multiperson coupon-collector variance coefficient. The present claim identifies the strictly ordered *entire* quantile-width profile for every sample size and noninteger effective exponent. This is not a re-expression of the known variance inequality: it gives a simultaneous coupling of all two-observation absolute gaps, yielding every increasing distance-risk comparison. It is a motivated structural strengthening and natural extension to the power-CDF family, not a numerical variant or a reprinted theorem.
